notes.notes:

We will continue to work on AI behaviour and other bugs for the next update!

notes.title: Dev Diary Begins...
notes.notes:
We are glad to share with you our first dev diary, which is hosted over on YouTube.

These are planned to be released on a weekly or bi-weekly basis, and we hope they will contribute to us building a community around BAD BLOOD: 1926, maybe even make us some money, and generally be entertaining as well...

Highlights include discussion of our upcoming Kickstarter efforts, why anyone should bother making a dev diary at all, and a few callouts of less than favourable characters in the games industry.

notes.title: Weapon and AI improvements, with more bugfixes
notes.notes:
One of our favourite bug fixes lets players pickup the switchblade, which was previously falling through floor, never to be seen again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935952/6d17f592f2a995ce13e361a648f0d50170e0a56c.jpg[/img]

As well as fixing some bugs, we made some changes to AI behaviour, sped up the animations for changing weapon, and tweaked auto-switching. We've tried to tweak the AI so that it is less likely to shoot you in the back from miles away, at least on the easier settings.

We have also added a few more rewards for players who explore more thoroughly, and removed some of the more dangerous enemies from easier settings - since we never intended them to be there anyway.

[*] Enemies will sometimes not move, can be worked around by restarting the level
[*] An intended speed run route skips a checkpoint

[/list]

notes.title: Graphics quality, FOV settings and framerate...
notes.notes:
Feedback on our demo from players inspired us to add quality settings and an FOV slider to the graphics options in the main and in-game menus. Hopefully this will improve the experience for all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44935952/d644afca560951b37458d55d3589e0bb9f68686b.png[/img]

Whilst improving the framerate without altering quality would be the ideal, we realise that we should have made quality settings available from the start.

That being said, we have also improved the baseline framerate with some improved culling and physics settings, so that things are faster without looking any different!

notes.title: Our demo is going to land soon!
notes.notes:
This demo is the [i]vertical slice[/i] we have been showing publishers and investors, and will continue to do so, to try and secure funding to complete the game's development.

The term vertical slice comes from imagining the player's progress through a game along a timeline from left-to-right (or right-to-left).

This means that it should show complete and polished functionality for a short section of the game. This equates to finishing a significant chunk of the game's development.

It necessarily contains some horizontal slices, e.g. a weapon in the game will be used throughout this timeline, as will other features like enemy behaviours, player movement, pickups, and power-ups.

We still have about 2 years to go before release, assuming we can fulfill our funding goals...

So, why are we releasing this to the public at such an early stage?

We are hoping that we can engage with interested players to build the game [i]they[/i] want, and not just the game that [i]we[/i] want. The sooner we release something that people can criticise or show love for, the more we can do towards creating something truly beautiful and enjoyable.
